title: Biodesix to Showcase MRD Strategy at the Association for Molecular Pathology (AMP) 2026 Annual Meeting
summary: New data highlighting proprietary bioinformatics, ultrasensitive molecular detection, and collaborations with Bio-Rad Laboratories and Thermo Fisher Scientific to advance scalable MRD solutions for clinical laboratories LOUISVILLE, Colo., Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Biodesix, Inc.
body_markdown:
### New data highlighting proprietary bioinformatics, ultrasensitive molecular detection, and collaborations with Bio-Rad Laboratories and Thermo Fisher Scientific to advance scalable MRD solutions for clinical laboratories


LOUISVILLE, Colo., Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Biodesix, Inc. (Nasdaq: BDSX), a leading diagnostic solutions company, today announced it will present new data from its tumor-informed and tumor-naïve molecular monitoring programs at the Association for Molecular Pathology (AMP) 2026 Annual Meeting, November 10-14, 2026, in Seattle, Washington. Biodesix will present three posters and host a Corporate Workshop featuring speakers from its collaborators Bio-Rad Laboratories and Thermo Fisher Scientific.


The presentations build on the two complementary molecular residual disease (MRD) programs Biodesix[announced in September 2026](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=IxMLMd4Nl_6fqMnDMUuDKbtH2sDJG7PQDDlStTut_kltM9QbxjpDT5X5o2V2wF3uAXBVS1ADHj2QyXr4Fhds4gBkkNQEI_MErwl9NlLvTiLELK7RDN3i_X7MViMzMlJjIWyY_s0j59wlh8KZNgCfYYUZyBI_LfZxPyqsoFlrUe8oQaTRNNNDv1Lu1JdWfkTb2ZJp0sG6aH8hn8RSNTgWw7Y_75k5cfxFSpUHmyQOfdc=) : a tumor-informed solution developed with Bio-Rad Laboratories, which uses the Biodesix Diagnostic Cortex® bioinformatics platform to identify patient-specific tumor alterations and Droplet Digital™ PCR (ddPCR™) to track them in blood, and a tumor-naïve, methylation-based solution under development with Thermo Fisher Scientific on the Ion Torrent™ Genexus™ platform, which requires no tumor tissue. Both programs are designed to run on partner platforms already installed in laboratories around the world, an access model intended to bring advanced MRD testing to more laboratories and the patients they serve. Both approaches are being validated in collaboration with investigators at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK).


“MRD is one of the most important and rapidly evolving areas in oncology, and Biodesix is building capabilities across the full spectrum of that opportunity,” said Scott Hutton, Chief Executive Officer, Biodesix. “At AMP, we will showcase complementary tumor-informed and tumor-naïve approaches, novel bioinformatics capabilities, and a scalable laboratory access model designed to bring advanced MRD testing to more patients. We believe improving both test performance and patient access will be critical to the future adoption of MRD testing.”


“AMP brings together the laboratory professionals who will put these assays into practice, which makes it the ideal setting to share our MRD pipeline update and data,” said Gary Pestano, Ph.D., Chief Scientific Officer, Biodesix. “Sensitivity matters, and so does patient access. The work we are presenting in collaboration with our partners spans tumor-informed monitoring, tumor-naïve methylation detection, and novel bioinformatics approaches that make personalized testing faster and more efficient.”


**Biodesix Corporate Workshop**


**Listening for the Whisper: Monitoring Residual Disease and Emerging Resistance in the Blood**
Wednesday, November 11, 2026, 4:00 PM PT


Speakers from Bio-Rad Laboratories, Thermo Fisher Scientific, and Biodesix will discuss complementary approaches to detecting circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), which can signal that a cancer remains or is returning before it is visible on imaging.


- Prithwish Pal, Ph.D., Director, Global Product Management - Oncology, Bio-Rad Laboratories, will describe tumor-informed MRD monitoring, in which patient-specific variants identified from tumor tissue are tracked in blood with Droplet Digital™ PCR.
- José Luís Costa, Ph.D., Global Director Scientific Affairs, Clinical Next-Generation Sequencing and Oncology, Thermo Fisher Scientific, and Dr. Christopher Mueller, President & CEO, mDETECT, will present new tools for detecting methylation signatures in plasma on the Genexus™ platform. Because this approach does not require tumor tissue, it could extend molecular monitoring to patients whose tissue samples are unavailable or insufficient.
- Gary Pestano, Ph.D., Chief Scientific Officer, Biodesix, will present data from clinical specimens using both MRD approaches. He will also show how the same ultrasensitive ddPCR™ expertise applies to monitoring emerging resistance, using the GeneStrat® ESR1 ddPCR™ Test, a laboratory-developed test that detects 11 ESR1 mutations in plasma from patients with metastatic breast cancer.


Attendees will gain a practical view of molecular monitoring approaches across solid tumor settings, including the validation studies laboratories need to conduct before bringing ctDNA monitoring assays into clinical use. Carolyn Reifsnyder, MBT, Vice President of Strategic R&D Initiatives, Biodesix, will introduce and moderate the session.


**Biodesix Presentations**


**Scalable Bioinformatics for Assay Design Poster**
Presenter: Emma Longshore, Bioinformatician, Biodesix | Friday, November 13, 2026, 9:15-10:15 AM PT | Poster I020


This poster details a scalable, tissue-independent bioinformatics framework for rapidly designing personalized ddPCR-based MRD assays from existing sequencing data. The *in-silico* approach minimizes the need for additional tissue sampling and supports faster delivery of cost-effective monitoring tools for patients.


**Ultrasensitive, WGS-Informed MRD Detection Poster**
Presenter: Leisa Jackson, Staff Scientist, Biodesix | Saturday, November 14, 2026, 9:15-10:15 AM PT | Poster ST011


This poster describes a whole-genome sequencing (WGS)-informed workflow used to design and deploy bespoke multiplexed ddPCR™ assays. Building on data first presented at AACR 2026, the work shows MRD assays designed with the Biodesix Diagnostic Cortex® platform to track both single nucleotide variants (SNVs) and structural variants (SVs), demonstrating the platform’s ability to identify and follow complex, patient-specific tumor alterations.


**Advancements in Tumor-Naïve, Methylation-Based MRD Poster**
Presenter: Kristen Eller, Senior Scientist, Biodesix | Saturday, November 14, 2026, 9:15-10:15 AM PT | Poster ST147


This poster presents data from the Biodesix collaboration with Thermo Fisher Scientific on a tumor-naïve, methylation-based MRD solution using plasma from whole blood collected and shipped in stabilizer tubes.


**Biodesix Corporate Workshop Presentations** will be held at Arch at 800 Pike, Seattle Convention Center. Biodesix Development Services team members will also be at booth 544 to discuss end-to-end translational research, biomarker discovery, and clinical trial diagnostic solutions.
